title: Split routing graph and migrate counted resources to for_each to reduce plan churn
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Several networking blueprints currently use count() and positional indexes for route tables, subnets, and Route53 private zones which has caused frequent plan churn, unsafe resource renames during scale events, and brittle cross-region dependencies. This ticket refactors the routing/zone modules to expose explicit resource keys (for_each) and splits the monolithic routing graph into a lightweight central router module + region-specific staging modules. The change aims to: reduce noisy drift/plan diffs, make state mutations explicit for safer imports, and enable provider version upgrade (aws v5 -> v6) with minimal rollout risk.
background: Observed recurring failures: large terraform plans when adding/removing subnets, intermittent apply timeouts caused by provider v5 API rate differences, and several incidents where count index shifts led to accidental recreation of NAT gateways in production. Root causes: positional indexing (count) used for multi-az resources, tightly coupled module interfaces that returned lists, and mixed use of aws provider versions across workspaces.
acceptance_criteria: All routing-related modules converted from count/list interfaces to for_each with stable string keys
No terraform plans in staging or canary show resource replacements due to index shifts for common scale operations
Provider pinned to a single compatible version across infra repos and validated in CI (terraform validate + plan)
Migration guide and automated state-move plan created and rehearsed in staging workspace
At least one production region migrated with rollback tested and documented
migration_steps: Create new module interfaces that accept maps with explicit keys instead of lists
Add wrapper compatibility layer that accepts legacy list input and emits map with deterministic keys
In staging workspace: apply compatibility layer and run terraform plan to collect planned state moves
Use 'terraform state mv' scripted helper to move individual resources (NATs, route tables, route53 zones) to new keys
Smoke test network connectivity and cross-account peering after each move
Promote changes to canary region; run perf/regression tests and cost checks
Rollout to remaining regions in waves with on-call support scheduled and rollback playbook ready
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: state move errors can orphan resources. Mitigation: run in staging first and keep state backups and quick reprovision scripts
Risk: provider v6 behavior changes may affect API calls. Mitigation: run acceptance suite against a pinned v6 candidate in a forked workspace and hold rollback to v5 if regressions found
Risk: long terraform plan times during migration. Mitigation: migrate small subset of resources per wave and precompute resource mappings with the helper script
testing_plan: Unit test new module interfaces with terraform-compliance and kitchen-terraform
Integration test in staging workspace using real-ish infra (dedicated staging VPC)
End-to-end connectivity tests: cross-AZ routing, NAT failover, Route53 private zone resolution
CI gate: disallow merge if 'terraform plan' for staging reports any replacements for non-migrated resources
